fullPassage: Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a slum after an economic recession. Businesses close their doors and building owners have left. The area is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to move out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and gang violence between young people becomes an everyday thing. Despair is on every street corner. One day, however, a gang called the Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its free meal and medical care programs, decides to stop fighting and instead persuade young people to unite and create a better community. They suggest a peace treaty. “This is for peace, men. The violence took away our brothers. We’re not gangsters anymore. We’ve got to make this town a better place to live.” Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never again will they use violence to solve their disputes. This is the Bronx in the New York of the early 1970s, where hip-hop music was born as a major part of a new culture of peace created by African Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop, now one of the world’s most dominant music genres, is a fascinating one. Let’s explore it. DJing, Breakdancing, and MCing After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought one another started partying together. Abandoned buildings and parking lots were used for events called block parties. What eventually emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with music, dance, art, and style. The most popular block parties were those hosted by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At this party, using two turntables at the same time, Herc played two copies of the same record and then switched between them to extend the drum section known as the break. No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing. The break section became the most anticipated part of a song. People would form dancer circles and use the break to show off their individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to dance in groups in the streets and build a street dance battle culture. DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked a friend to take the role of addressing the audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This separate role became MCing. The Origin of the Word Hip-Hop Then where did the word hip-hop originate from? Nobody knows the exact origin, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party. A young man at the party was about to join the army. His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, “Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop.” The crowd loved it. After that, MCs tried out new lines at parties like “Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop,” “I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you don’t stop.” Such lines became a standard part of rap and were included in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s Delight (1979), which was an immediate success. The new music and dancing spread very fast. There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence during the 1980s in New York. One police officer asked a boy on the street if he knew why. The boy said, “It’s because they’re dancing.” The Messages of Hip-Hop Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good time together and boasting about the ability of the DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the 1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice. The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance. People heard the social message while moving to the beat. <The Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect.” Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture. Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes. The phrase “something from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the message of respect is about both self-worth and respect for others. The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop cannot be emphasized strongly enough. Hip-Hop in the 21st Century “The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” presented to the UN on May 16th, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace. This document reminds us of hip-hop’s original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history. When hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another important event. It meant that hip-hop, which started as underground music, had become a major art form like classical music. If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and more people regard it as a powerful means to express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about change through social messages, and still be engaged with music and connected to others. With its unique and growing appeal, hip-hop continues to be a global phenomenon. Further Reading Rhyme in Rap A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics. First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud. My house is so big you cannot see the top Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an ending sound “op.” Second, words can rhyme within the same line. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example, They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round. When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions. ④ decides: 주어 a gang(하나)에 맞춰 동사에 -s를 붙인 decides가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 주어가 단수(gang violence)면 동사도 -s 붙은 단수형: becomes

② born: 'hip-hop music was born'은 '힙합 음악이 탄생했다'예요. 음악이 '태어나게 된' 것이라 be동사 뒤 과거분사 born(수동)으로 쓰니 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ started: 주어 the gangs에 이어지는 과거시제 동사 started가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 뒤 문장이 완전하고 앞이 장소면 관계부사 where (which는 불완전한 문장 앞)

❌ ② 원문 'There is no heating even in winter'(겨울에도 난방이 없다)와 일치해요.

questions.passage: The Origin of the Word Hip-Hop Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?  Nobody knows the exact origin, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party.  A young man at the party was about to join the army.  His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, “Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop. ” The crowd loved it.  After that, MCs tried out new lines at parties like “Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop,” “I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you don’t stop. ” Such lines became a standard part of rap and were included in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s Delight (1979), which was an immediate success.

questions.passage: Hip-Hop in the 21st Century “The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” presented to the UN on May 16th, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace.  This document reminds us of hip-hop’s original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history.  When hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another important event.  It meant that hip-hop, which started as underground music, had become a major art form like classical music.  If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and more people regard it as a powerful means to express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about change through social messages, and still be engaged with music and connected to others.

ch: 유엔에 제출된 그 평화 선언문은 힙합을 국제적 평화 문화로 공식 인정했다.
힙합은 주류 클래식 음악으로 출발해 점차 언더그라운드로 옮겨 갔다.
오늘날 힙합의 인기는 빠르게 식어 가고 있다.

questions.passage: Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a slum after an economic recession.  Businesses close their doors and building owners have left.  The area is full of abandoned buildings.  There is no heating even in winter.  Only those who can’t afford to move out remain.  Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and gang violence between young people becomes an everyday thing.  Despair is on every street corner.  One day, however, a gang called the Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its free meal and medical care programs, decides to stop fighting and instead persuade young people to unite and create a better community.  They suggest a peace treaty.  “This is for peace, men.  The violence took away our brothers.  We’re not gangsters anymore.  We’ve got to make this town a better place to live. ” Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty.  Never again will they use violence to solve their disputes.  This is the Bronx in the New York of the early 1970s, where hip-hop music was born as a major part of a new culture of peace created by African Americans and immigrants.  The story of hip-hop, now one of the world’s most dominant music genres, is a fascinating one.  Let’s explore it.  DJing, Breakdancing, and MCing After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought one another started partying together.  Abandoned buildings and parking lots were used for events called block parties.  What eventually emerged from these parties?  A vibrant youth movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti.  It replaced gang violence with music, dance, art, and style.  The most popular block parties were those hosted by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding father of hip-hop.  Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique.  At this party, using two turntables at the same time, Herc played two copies of the same record and then switched between them to extend the drum section known as the break.  No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.  Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.  The break section became the most anticipated part of a song.  People would form dancer circles and use the break to show off their individual dancing skills.  Kool Herc named the people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls.  These people began to dance in groups in the streets and build a street dance battle culture.  DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the crowd.  They would shout phrases like “To the beat” and “You don’t stop! ” This was the beginning of rapping or MCing.  When DJs couldn’t do both DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked a friend to take the role of addressing the audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their parties.  This separate role became MCing.  The Origin of the Word Hip-Hop Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?  Nobody knows the exact origin, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party.  A young man at the party was about to join the army.  His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, “Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop. ” The crowd loved it.  After that, MCs tried out new lines at parties like “Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop,” “I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you don’t stop. ” Such lines became a standard part of rap and were included in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s Delight (1979), which was an immediate success.  The new music and dancing spread very fast.  There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence during the 1980s in New York.  One police officer asked a boy on the street if he knew why.  The boy said, “It’s because they’re dancing. ” The Messages of Hip-Hop Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good time together and boasting about the ability of the DJ or the rapper.  However, a significant shift occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the 1980s.  Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking.  This song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen.  With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice.  The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s.  At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance.  People heard the social message while moving to the beat.  <The Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect. ” Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers.  For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture.  Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes.  The phrase “something from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources.  Rappers also proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in a similar way to the pioneers.  This is why the message of respect is about both self-worth and respect for others.  The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop cannot be emphasized strongly enough.  Hip-Hop in the 21st Century “The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” presented to the UN on May 16th, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace.  This document reminds us of hip-hop’s original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history.  When hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another important event.  It meant that hip-hop, which started as underground music, had become a major art form like classical music.  If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and more people regard it as a powerful means to express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about change through social messages, and still be engaged with music and connected to others.

det.analysis:
글은 갱단 폭력이 가득하던 브롱크스에서 평화 운동과 함께 힙합이 태어나, 오늘날 세계적 문화 현상으로 성장하기까지의 이야기를 담고 있어요.

✅ ① How Hip-Hop Rose from Gang Violence to a Global Culture(힙합이 갱단 폭력에서 세계적 문화로 성장한 과정) — 폭력에서 시작해 세계적 문화가 된 전체 흐름을 압축한 제목이에요. ←정답

det.korean: ② 'something from nothing'은 '무(無)에서 유(有)를 만들다'라는 뜻으로, 자원이 거의 없는 게토에서 새 문화를 창조했다는 의미
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'The phrase "something from nothing," ~ is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources'(이 표현은 자원이 매우 부족한 게토에서 새 문화를 만든 초기 힙합인에 대한 감탄의 표현이다). 'something from nothing'은 '아무것도 없는 데서 무언가를 만들어 내다'라는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① 다른 음악을 모방했다: '새로운 문화를 만들었다(developed a new culture)'는 원문과 반대예요.

✅ ② 자원이 거의 없는 환경에서 완전히 새로운 문화를 만들어 냈다: 'despite very limited resources(자원이 부족함에도)'와 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ 막대한 자본의 후원: 자원이 '부족했다'는 원문과 정반대예요.

❌ ④ 전통을 그대로 보존했다: '새 문화를 만들었다'는 내용과 반대예요.
det.tip: something from nothing = 무에서 유를 창조 (limited resources에도 새 문화 창조)

ch: 다른 지역의 유명한 음악을 그대로 모방하여 성장했다
자원이 거의 없는 환경에서 완전히 새로운 문화를 만들어 냈다
막대한 자본의 후원 덕분에 단숨에 유명해졌다
오래된 전통 음악을 그대로 이어받아 보존했다

questions.passage: “This is for peace, men.  The violence took away our brothers.  We’re not gangsters anymore.  We’ve got to make this town a better place to live. ” Thanks to <u>these new voices</u>, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 these new voices가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 게토 브라더스가 '이것은 평화를 위한 것이다 ~'라고 외친 평화의 호소를 가리킴
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty'(이 새로운 목소리들 덕분에, 그 지역 전역의 갱단 지도자들이 협정에 서명한다). 바로 앞에서 게토 브라더스가 'This is for peace, men. ~ We've got to make this town a better place to live.'라고 평화를 호소했어요. these new voices는 이 호소를 가리켜요.

❌ ① 이민자들의 목소리: 이민자는 뒤(브롱크스 설명)에 나오고, 협정을 이끈 호소와는 달라요.

❌ ② 라디오의 힙합 음악: 이 시점에는 아직 힙합이 등장하지 않았어요.

✅ ③ 게토 브라더스가 외친 평화의 호소: 앞 문장의 평화 선언이 지도자들의 서명을 이끌었어요. ←정답

❌ ④ 경찰의 공식 성명: 경찰이 발표했다는 내용은 본문에 없어요.
det.tip: 바로 앞의 'This is for peace ~'라는 평화 호소 = these new voices

questions.passage: The Origin of the Word Hip-Hop Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?  Nobody knows __________, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party.  A young man at the party was about to join the army.  His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, “Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① the exact origin(정확한 기원): hip-hop이라는 말이 어디서 왔는지 아무도 '정확한 기원'을 모른다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Nobody knows ___, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party'(아무도 ___ 모르지만, hip-hop이라는 말은 블록 파티에서 처음 쓰였다고 전해진다). 앞 문장 'where did the word hip-hop originate from?(그 말이 어디서 유래했을까?)'과 이어지므로, 그 말의 '기원'을 모른다는 뜻이 되어야 해요.

✅ ① the exact origin(정확한 기원): '어디서 유래했나'라는 물음과 딱 이어져요. ←정답

❌ ② the real singer(진짜 가수): 특정 가수를 찾는 내용이 아니에요.

❌ ③ the first album(첫 앨범): 앨범이 아니라 '단어의 유래'를 이야기하고 있어요.

❌ ④ the main reason(주된 이유): 이유가 아니라 '기원(출처)'을 모른다는 흐름이에요.
det.tip: 앞 문장 'where did the word hip-hop originate from?' → the exact origin(정확한 기원)

questions.passage: Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a slum after an economic recession.  Businesses close their doors and building owners have left.  The area is full of abandoned buildings.  __________.  Only those who can’t afford to move out remain.  Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and gang violence between young people becomes an everyday thing.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"겨울에도 난방이 전혀 되지 않는다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) even, heating, in, is, no, There, winter 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: There is no heating even in winter
det.analysis:
'~이 없다'는 'There is no ~'로 시작해요: There → is → no.

무엇이 없는가 하면 '난방(heating)'이에요: heating.

'~에도(심지어)'는 even으로 나타내고, '겨울에'는 in winter예요. 순서대로 even → in → winter를 붙여요.

이으면 There / is / no / heating / even / in / winter.
det.tip: There is no + 명사(heating) + even in ~(~에도): 겨울에도 난방이 없다

questions.wa: There is no heating even in winter
accept: There is no heating even in winter

questions.passage: Hip-Hop in the 21st Century “The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” ①<u>presenting</u> to the UN on May 16th, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace.  This document reminds us of hip-hop’s original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: presenting → presented: 선언문은 UN에 '제출되는' 대상이라 수동의 과거분사 presented
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 '"The HipHop Declaration of Peace," ①<u>presenting</u> to the UN on May 16th, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace'예요. '「힙합 평화 선언문」은 5월 16일 UN에 제출되어, 힙합을 국제적 평화 문화로 공식 인정했다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 The Declaration(선언문)은 스스로 제출하는 주체가 아니라, 누군가에 의해 UN에 '제출되는' 대상이에요. 이렇게 '~되다/~당하다'를 나타낼 때는 과거분사(p.p.)로 꾸며 줘요.

present(제출하다)의 과거분사는 presented예요. 그래서 능동의 presenting이 아니라 수동의 presented(제출된)로 고쳐야 맞아요. 뒤의 'to the UN(UN에)'도 이 부분이 수동임을 알려 주는 신호예요.
det.tip: 명사가 동작을 '당하는' 대상이면 과거분사: (was) presented to the UN

questions.passage: ” Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers.  For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture.  __________.  The phrase “something from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그러므로 많은 힙합 아티스트들은 이 영웅들을 아무리 존경해도 지나치지 않다는 데 동의한다." (14단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) agree, cannot, for, have, heroes, hip-hoppers, many, much, respect, that, Therefore, these, they, too 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 14단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Therefore many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes
det.analysis:
'그러므로'는 Therefore로 문장을 열어요: Therefore.

주어와 동사를 놓아요. '많은 힙합 아티스트들이 ~에 동의한다'이므로 many → hip-hoppers → agree.

무엇에 동의하는지 that절로 이어요: that → they. '아무리 ~해도 지나치지 않다'는 'cannot have too much ~(아무리 ~해도 지나치지 않다)' 구문으로 나타내요: cannot → have → too → much → respect.

'누구에게'는 for these heroes로 마무리해요: for → these → heroes.

이으면 Therefore / many / hip-hoppers / agree / that / they / cannot / have / too / much / respect / for / these / heroes.
det.tip: cannot have too much ~ = 아무리 ~해도 지나치지 않다 (강한 강조 구문)

questions.wa: Therefore many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes
accept: Therefore many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes
Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes

questions.passage: DJing, Breakdancing, and MCing __________.  Abandoned buildings and parking lots were used for events called block parties.  What eventually emerged from these parties?  A vibrant youth movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti.  It replaced gang violence with music, dance, art, and style.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"평화 협정 이후, 서로 싸우던 갱단들이 함께 파티를 열기 시작했다."

[ After / another / fought / gangs / had / one / partying / peace / started / that / the / the / together / treaty ] (14단어) (영어로)

det.korean: After the peace treaty the gangs that had fought one another started partying together
det.analysis:
'평화 협정 이후'라는 시간 표현으로 시작해요: After → the → peace → treaty.

주어는 '갱단들'이에요: the → gangs. 어떤 갱단인지 관계대명사 that으로 꾸며 줘요. '서로 싸웠던'은 파티를 연 것보다 먼저라 과거완료 had fought로 씁니다: that → had → fought → one → another.

마지막으로 '함께 파티를 열기 시작했다'를 놓아요. start 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써서 started partying, '함께'는 together로 마무리해요: started → partying → together.

이으면 After / the / peace / treaty / the / gangs / that / had / fought / one / another / started / partying / together.
det.tip: start + 동명사(started partying) = ~하기 시작하다 / that had fought one another(서로 싸웠던)가 gangs를 꾸밈

questions.wa: After the peace treaty the gangs that had fought one another started partying together
accept: After the peace treaty the gangs that had fought one another started partying together
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought one another started partying together

questions.passage: With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice.  The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s.  At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance.  __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"사람들은 비트에 맞춰 몸을 움직이면서 사회적 메시지를 들었다." (10단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) beat, heard, message, moving, People, social, the, the, to, while 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: People heard the social message while moving to the beat
det.analysis:
'사람들은 ~을 들었다'가 핵심이라 '주어(People) + 동사(heard)'로 시작해요: People → heard.

무엇을 들었는지 목적어를 놓아요. '사회적 메시지'라서 the → social → message.

'~하면서'는 while + -ing(분사구문)로 나타내요. '몸을 움직이면서'이니 while → moving. '비트에 맞춰'는 to the beat로 마무리해요: to → the → beat.

이으면 People / heard / the / social / message / while / moving / to / the / beat.
det.tip: while + 동명사(while moving) = ~하면서 / to the beat = 비트에 맞춰

questions.wa: People heard the social message while moving to the beat
accept: People heard the social message while moving to the beat
